title: Pointwise threshold representation inequality
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ and $g$ be functions from $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to $\\{-1,1\\}$, and let $p:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$ satisfy $f(x)=1$ when $p(x)\\ge 0$ and $f(x)=-1$ when $p(x)<0$ for every $x$. Suppose also that $p(x)\\ne 0$ for every $x$. Then for every $x\\in\\{-1,1\\}^n$, $g(x)p(x)\\le f(x)p(x)$, and if $g(x)\\ne f(x)$, then $g(x)p(x)<f(x)p(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is the threshold sign of $p$ at every input
